title: Browser overworld_session_id "ui-journey" is retyped in its own regression, so changing it stays green
body:
The browser's `overworld_session_id` is the bare literal `"ui-journey"`, and the test that
covers it feeds in its own copy rather than importing the one the app uses — so changing
it leaves the suite green while silently rehashing every browser quest state.

Found while closing intake `407d606a0e9cbafc`. That ticket's blocker (a) was "no
deterministic browser overworld_session_id exists, and one is required because it is
hashed into quest state". The blocker was discharged in `442a06b9` (2026-08-30) by
stamping a fixed literal, which is a correct and deliberate fix — determinism is exactly
what was needed. This is the seam it left behind, not a complaint about the choice.

  ui/src/App.tsx:915
    const launchOverlay = embeddedLaunchOverlayForPlan(plan, "ui-journey");

  tests/regression/embedded_launch_overlay_parity.test.ts:153
    const launchOverlay = embeddedLaunchOverlayForPlan(plan, "ui-journey");

Those are the ONLY two occurrences in the repo (`grep -rn '"ui-journey"'`, excluding
node_modules). The test does not import the value from `App.tsx`; it re-types it. So the
two agree today by coincidence of authorship, and nothing enforces that they keep
agreeing.

WHY IT MATTERS

The id is hashed into quest state through the launch-overlay receipt, so it is not a
label — it is part of the identity of every quest a browser player starts. Retyping it,
renaming it to something more descriptive, or making it per-session would change
`stateHash` for every browser journey. The parity regression would keep passing, because
it would be asserting a round-trip over its own private literal rather than over the
app's.

This is the same failure shape the repo already rejects elsewhere: a documented or
duplicated constant that agrees with its source only by hand. Compare
`blind-tester/implemented-launch-paths.json`, which exists precisely so `run.sh` and
`bin/doctor.ts` cannot drift, and `tests/regression/playtest_loop_documented_cohort.test.ts`,
which checks a documented value against the derivation instead of pinning a copy.

FIX

Export the id as a named constant beside `embeddedLaunchOverlayForPlan` — it belongs with
the function that consumes it — and have both `App.tsx` and the parity test import it.
One line each, and the coincidence becomes a dependency.

Worth a quick sweep at the same time for other cross-boundary literals shared between
`ui/src` and `tests/` by retyping rather than import.

evidence.summary: Only two occurrences; the parity test re-types the literal instead of importing it, and the id is hashed into every browser quest state
